retracted.notice: Notice of retraction, Clinical Dermatology Review 5(2):263, Jul-Dec 2021, doi:10.4103/2542-551X.324588
retracted.note: Retracted by the journal as a duplicate of the same authors' 2020 article (J Pak Assoc Dermatol 2020;30(2):261-266). Its 2 ledger rows were removed on 2026-11-28 with Ben's approval (00:57 UTC) and replaced by data/staging/rajegowda2020.json. Kept for history; tools/ledger.py merge skips any record with this block.

rows.assessment_method: grading of improvement in pigmentation, assessed monthly for 3 months: Grade 1 <25% no response, Grade 2 26-50% minimal, Grade 3 51-75% good, Grade 4 >75% excellent; assessor, blinding and whether clinical or photographic not in abstract

rows.time_from_last_treatment: NOT_DERIVABLE: the abstract reports results 'At the end of the treatment period' and gives time only from the start (monthly assessments for 3 months); treatment was repeated monthly 'till the repigmentation for maximum of 3 applications', so the number of applications and the date of each macule's final application are not reported
rows.complete_match: not in abstract (highest reported grade is >75% improvement, which is partial)
rows.attrition: [5] of 30 enrolled patients did not complete (30 selected, 25 completed); reasons not in abstract
rows.citation: Rajegowda HM, Kalegowda D, Madegowda SB, Rangarajaiah AC. Efficacy and safety of 88% phenol application versus cryotherapy in repigmentation of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis: a prospective study. Clin Dermatol Rev 2021;5(1):49-53
rows.intervention: short contact cryotherapy, single cryotherapy application of 3-5 s per macule, once a month until repigmentation, maximum 3 applications
rows.comparator: 88% phenol applied to 5 other IGH macules of the same patient
rows.arm_result: 75/125 (60%) macules excellent (>75% improvement); 20/125 (16%) good (51-75%); [30/125 (24%)] minimal or no response combined (not reported separately); P < 0.05 vs phenol (comparison not specified)
rows.texture_or_scar: not in abstract as counts; abstract states persistent scabbing and ulceration were more common with 88% phenol than with cryotherapy
rows.uncertainty: Abstract only. No untreated control macules are in the abstract, although every patient had more than 10 macules [so spontaneous change cannot be separated from treatment effect]. Within-patient comparison: each patient contributes 5 macules to each arm, and the abstract does not say how macules were allocated, who graded them, whether grading was blinded, or whether the P < 0.05 test accounted for clustering within patients; the test's comparison (which grade or grades) is not stated. 125 = [25 completers x 5 macules], so [the results appear to cover completers only; the 25 macules per arm of the 5 patients who did not complete appear not to be included]. The grading scale as printed leaves gaps but no overlap: Grade 1 is '<25%' and Grade 2 '26%–50%', so 25% falls in no grade, and Grade 2 ends at 50% while Grade 3 starts at 51%. Grade 1 ('no response') covers everything below 25%. Minimal and no-response counts are not in abstract. The schedule sentence is ambiguous: 'single cryotherapy for 3-5 s was applied for another 5 IGH macules once in a month till the repigmentation for maximum of 3 applications' can be read as applying the monthly, up-to-3 schedule to cryotherapy only or to both arms; the number of applications each macule received is not reported, so time from each macule's final treatment cannot be derived. Results are given only 'At the end of the treatment period'; no visit after treatment ended is in the abstract, so durability is not in abstract. The conclusion calls cryotherapy 'more efficacious and safe', but side effects are described only qualitatively (no counts). Duplicate-cohort check: the abstract gives no study site, recruitment dates or ethics approval, so overlap with other cohorts cannot be settled from this text. The authors' department (Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences) and three author names (Rajegowda, Kalegowda/Deepadarshan, Madegowda/Shashikumar) are shared with deepadarshan2023 in the ledger, whose own source (papers/excerpts/deepadarshan2023.txt, not this text) reports a different treatment (308 nm excimer laser) run from August 2022 to January 2023, after this article's 2021 publication [so the two are probably not the same cohort, although individual patients could recur; this abstract gives no dates or patient details to check]. The earlier lead note's 'near-identical title' article in J Pak Assoc Dermatol was not identified in this source text.

quotes.quote: A total of 30 patients with more than 10 IGH macules were selected.
A total of 25 patients completed the study.
For each enrolled patient, 88% phenol was applied to 5 IGH macules and single cryotherapy for 3–5 s was applied for another 5 IGH macules
once in a month till the repigmentation for maximum of 3 applications. Patients were assessed monthly for 3 months for the side effects and improvement in pigmentation.

The degree of improvement in pigmentation was assessed using a grading system, <25% - no response (Grade-1), 26%–50% - minimal (Grade-2), 51%–75% - good (Grade-3), and >75% - excellent response (Grade-4).
Side effects such as persistent scabbing, ulceration were more common with 88% phenol application compared to cryotherapy.
Department of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprosy, Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences, Mandya, Karnataka, India

verifier.notes: Verifier 2, 2026-11-27, source papers/excerpts/rajegowda2021.txt (ABSTRACT_ONLY). 0 failed cells (rows counted from 0). Checked every cell of rows 0 and 1 against the source: all quotes verbatim (validator ok); counts 30 enrolled, 25 completed, 125 macules per arm, cryotherapy 75 (60%) excellent and 20 (16%) good, phenol 37 (29.6%) excellent and 29 (23.2%) good match the Results; bracketed remainders [30/125 (24%)] and [59/125 (47.2%)], [150] per arm and [5] non-completers are correct arithmetic and bracketed; time_from_last_treatment and months_after_final_tx NOT_DERIVABLE is right (results only 'At the end of the treatment period', assessment timed from start, number of applications not reported); analysis_unit lesion with clustering caveat; outcome_tier partial_repigmentation (>75% is not complete coverage); scabbing and ulceration recorded qualitatively, scarring and dark overshoot marked 'not in abstract'; grading-scale wording now says gaps but no overlap, which matches the source; schedule ambiguity, lack of untreated control, allocation, assessor, blinding and completer-only denominator are in uncertainty. Observation, not a failed cell: the deepadarshan2023 excerpt (reference 15) cites an earlier paper by the same group, 'Efficacy and safety of 10,600 nm fractional carbon dioxide laser versus 88% phenol in treatment of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis: A prospective study', J Dermatol Dermatol Surg 2022;26(1):1, which may share phenol-arm patients with this study; worth a duplicate-cohort check by the orchestrator.
